To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the parallel K means algorithm can benefit from an efficient island model and that it can be highly scalable.

the K means algorithm is an excellent test case for the optimization of parallel algorithms in general and that parallel programming requires more than the simple balance of computation and communications.

(1) The island version of the K means parallel algorithm outperforms its master slave counterpart by an order of magnitude, (2) The use of a mathematical library can have a significant negative impact on the performance of an algorithm and (3) The use of high precision profiling tools can reveal performance bottlenecks that would otherwise remain hidden and unaccounted for.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the k means algorithm for the purpose of using it in a genetic algorithm.
the parallel optimization and scalability of the K means clustering algorithm.
the parallelization and optimization of the K Means clustering algorithm in two distinct parallel execution environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parallel processing is a very complicated task that requires the expertise and the tools to address it in a systematic and precise manner.
the K means algorithm can be optimized to achieve a high degree of scalability and efficiency on both Beowulf clusters and SMP machines.

the optimization of the parallel version of a serial algorithm can be more complex than the algorithm itself and that a thorough understanding of the parallel execution environments is essential to its optimization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parallel programming is a complex task requiring multidisciplinary expertise and that the parallelization process is a continuous optimization process.
parallel performance tuning is a multidisciplinary task requiring a mixture of theoretical, experimental and empirical knowledge of both the parallel algorithm and execution environment.
parallel performance optimization is not a trivial task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parallel programming is a very complex endeavor that requires an in depth knowledge of the parallel execution environments.
a thorough understanding of the execution environment, the program and its data representation is a prerequisite to any attempt at parallel optimization.
a multidisciplinary approach is needed to achieve high efficiency.
